title: GNSBI and NESBp Knowledge Sharing Platform
text: This platform is in development under the Northern European Sea Basins project (NESBp). It is supporting the Greater North Sea Basin Initiative (GNSBI). GNSBI is a framework for collaboration between nine countries from the North Sea region, to strengthen cooperation on maritime spatial planning (MSP).

title: GNSBI and NESBp Knowledge Sharing Platform
text:
How it works
At the top of this page, you can choose the type of entry to the portal (policy maker / MSP expert / Sectorial actors). When this is chose, you choose the type of information that you are interested in at the left side panel (MSP input / Knowledge base / MSP zoning). This opens up a menu where more specific information layers can be chosen.

title: GNSBI and NESBp Knowledge Sharing Platform
text:
Credits
The platform is developed by Deltares, with input from NESBp WP5 (Knowledge Transfer & Sharing) partners in close collaboration with GNSBI. Comments and input from OSPAR, HELCOM, Technical Expert Group (TEG) on Data for MSP, and the eMSP project were highly appreciated.

title: Exclusive Economic Zones
text: Maritime Boundaries and Exclusive Economic Zones from the VLIZ Maritime Boundaries Geodatabase. Boundaries have been built using information about treaties between coastal countries. When treaties are not available, median lines have been calculated. An exclusive economic zone (EEZ) is a sea zone extending from a state’s coast or baseline over which the state has special rights over the exploration and use of marine resources. Generally a state’s EEZ extends 200 nautical miles out from its coast, except where resulting points would be closer to another country. This dataset also contains delimitation of overlapping claims, court rulings and joint regimes. Flanders Marine Institute (2023). Maritime Boundaries Geodatabase: Maritime Boundaries and Exclusive Economic Zones (200NM), version 12. Available online at https://www.marineregions.org/. https://doi.org/10.14284/632

title: Multi-use
text:
This map is a first exploration between the collaboration of the GNSBI Knowledge Sharing and Multi-Use working tracks. The map presents multi-use case studies in the North Sea based on the publication Expert Study on Ocean Multi-use in the German Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of the North and Baltic Sea by s.Pro – sustainable projects GmbH. These locations are pilot projects and not running multi-use operations, the case studies of the study are not included.
Each multi-use activity is represented by one colour in the pie chart. Each colour represents always two activities:Offshore Wind Energy and Any other activity (refer to legend).
Disclaimer: This map is a work in progress. Not all multi-use locations listed in the expert study could be mapped due to missing coordinates or information about the location.

title: Long-term Perspective of Fisheries
text: The outputs generated by the WT Fisheries include aggregated fisheries data (2018-2022) from Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweden. These countries, as well as Ireland and Norway, supplied information on MPAs and offshore renewables and the fisheries management within such areas. The EU Commission compiled this information for the UK EEZ. In the maps, values are only shown if more than 5 unique vessels are present during the selected time-period, otherwise the values are greyed out.

title: Shipping
text:
NaviSafe (SHOM) is a MSP tool which provides a macroscopic view on potential maritime traffic risks with different activities and sea uses. The tool is currently under development.
The risk calculation is vased on a risk matrix per vesel type and activity, which was developed based on expert judgement and literature review.
Step 1: Collision Risk calculation was performed per vessel type with the ReMAP NaviSafe Tool. Risk Index output ranges from 0 (low risk) to 4 (high risk).
Step 2: Vessel type risk maps were summed to a Cumulative Risk Index to showcase the cumulative collision risk for all vessel types with OWF.
